free_tier.stated: no free tier and no signup credit: a prepaid balance from a USD 5 minimum top-up, spent per minute on GPU rentals at list rates, with the A100 80G at USD 1.59/hr and the RTX 4090 24G at USD 0.39/hr. From 3 November 2026 a single top-up of USD 100 or more earns a USD 10 bonus, once per account.

per_object_cap.notes: the ceiling that matters is the card chosen on the deploy page

retention.stated: Destroying an instance deletes everything stored on it, and an instance is destroyed if the balance runs out.
retention.notes: a machine record: what is lost is the instance and its local storage; copy results off before the instance ends

egress.terms: no egress charges: the vendor states 'No hidden fees. No egress charges. Stop anytime.'
egress.free_allowance: unmetered: no egress charge is stated

interface_detail: root SSH and JupyterLab on the instance templates, and an OpenAI-compatible API at https://cloudgpu.app/v1 for the per-token models; read from the vendor pages, not probed
tooling: root SSH and JupyterLab on every instance; one-click templates from the console; an MCP server that lets an MCP client quote a price, rent a GPU after approval, run a job and shut the GPU down
chaining: none: no free lane to chain. The smallest purchase is a USD 5 top-up, and results must be copied off the instance before it is destroyed.

limits.value: prepaid balance only: no signup credit, a USD 5 minimum top-up, and instances are destroyed when the balance reaches zero

limits_note: the binding count is the prepaid balance; nothing is free, so the cost of one run is the list rate multiplied by the minutes billed
binding_note: the binding count is the prepaid balance: there is no free allowance, the minimum top-up is USD 5 and a balance of zero destroys the instance

identity_cost.detail: Sign-up is an email address or a Google account and no phone number is needed. There is no signup credit, so use needs a prepaid top-up of at least USD 5 by card, by USDT on TRC-20, or by bank transfer for business customers.

reliability_note: the vendor page states a public beta with no uptime guarantee and no service credits; capacity is sourced from third-party suppliers and the supplier behind an instance can change
